spans.s:
यत् 1. यत्, यन्, यती, यत् (fr. rt. 5. इ),
going, passing, moving.

यत् 2. यत् (connected with rt. यम्), cl.
1. A. (Ved. and ep. also P.) यतते (-ति),
येते (3rd pl. येतिरे), यतिष्यते, अयतिष्ट, यति-
तुम्, to join, connect, unite (Ved. P.); to excite,
arouse (Ved. P., according to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda

. यतति = यातयति, प्रवर्तयति, he arouses,
animates to exertion); to join or attach one's self to,
unite one's self with, associate with (Ved. A.); to
come together or be arranged in order (Ved. A.);
to proceed, go (Ved.); to try to join one's self with
(with loc.); to endeavour to reach (Ved. A.); to
strive or endeavour after, struggle after, be eager or
anxious for (with loc. or dat. or even acc., or with
one of the following prepositional words, अर्थे,
अर्थाय, अर्थम्, हेतोस्, प्रति, or with the inf.);
to exert one's self, endeavour, take pains, make
effort, persevere, observe caution, be watchful; to
strive against, be engaged in mutual contest, contend
together (Ved.): Caus. यातयति, -यते, -यितुम्,
Aor. अयीयतत्, to join, connect, associate, unite
(Ved. P.); to join or attach one's self to (Ved. A.);
to join or unite to (Ved. P.); to requite, recompense,
repay, restore, return, give up; to cause to be repaid
or requited or restored; to receive in requital (A.);
to cause to strive or make effort, animate, encourage,
instigate; to cause to contend (Ved.); to pain,
harass, distress, torture, vex, annoy; to reprehend,
despise: Desid. यियतिषते: Intens. यायत्यते,
यायत्ति; [cf. according to some Gr. ζητέω.]

1. यात्, यान्, याती or यान्ती, यात् (for 2. यात् see
s.v.), going, proceeding, moving; that which moves
(e. g. Ṛg-veda

, इन्द्रो यातो ऽवसितस्य राजा,
Indra the sovereign of all that is movable and im-
movable).
—यात्-सत्त्र, अम्, n., Ved. ‘continuing
sacrifice,’ N. of certain solemn ceremonies which go
on for a long period, (also called Sārasvata.)

यात् 2. यात्, ind. (properly obsolete abl. fr.
the pronom. base 3. य, cf. तात्; for 1. यात् see p. 813,
col. 2, for 3. यात् see below), inasmuch as, so far as,
so long as, since, (but according to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda
1. 80, 15, यात् = यान्तम्, pervading;

, यात्
= यातः = गच्छतः, passing;

, यात् =
यानि [कर्माणि], which [actions]; according to
some यात् is an interjection of pleasure; of alarm; of
restlessness.)
—याच्-छ्रेष्ठ, अस्, आ, अम् (i. e. यात्
+ श्रेष्ठ), Ved. the best possible; [cf. यावच्-
छ्रेष्ठ; but according to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda

, यात् is a separate word, and means ‘an
enemy,’ as if fr. rt. 2. यत्.]

यात् 3. यात् (fr. rt. 2. यत्), in ऋण-यात्, Ved.
the avenger of guilt or debt.

यतत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, exerting one's self, striving
after, &c., (in Ṛg-veda

. यतत् = उद्ध-
रत्, extirpating.)

यतन, अम्, n. the act of making effort or exertion,
an effort, endeavour.

यतान, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. uniting or coming to-
gether (in regular order), ranging; proceeding, (Sāy.
= प्रवर्तमान.)

यातन यातन, अम्, n. (fr. the Caus. of rt.
2. यत्), the act of requiting, requital, retaliation,
recompense, reward, return; वैरस्य यातनम्,
requital of hostile acts, revenge, vengeance; (आ), f.
requital, (यातनाम् दा, to make requital, revenge);
recompense, retaliation, reward [cf. वैर-य्˚]; acute
pain, torment, anguish, agony, (especially) punish-
ment inflicted by Yama, the pains of hell; personified
as the daughter of Fear (भय) and Death (मृत्यु).
—यातनार्थीय (˚ना-अर्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, fit for tor-
ment, capable of suffering, susceptible of the pains of
hell.

यतनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be exerted or persevered
or striven after; (the neut. may be used impersonally,
[]
e. g. सदा यतनीयम् मुक्तौ, one must always
strive after final emancipation.)

यतमान, अस्, आ, अम्, striving, endeavouring,
struggling, persevering, making effort, taking pains.

यतव्य, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. an unused यतु), Ved. =
प्रयत्न-वत्.

1. यातव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be gone or set out, to
be marched; to be gone against, to be assailed or
attacked, (the neuter is used impersonally.)

2. यातव्य, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. 2. यातु below), service-
able against witchcraft, keeping off Rākṣasas.
यातव्य यातव्य. See p. 813, col. 2.

यतित, अस्, आ, अम्, striven, endeavoured, attempted,
tried, striven after, (sometimes with inf. used pas-
sively, e. g. एष त्वया हन्तुं यतितः, he was
attempted to be killed by thee); endeavouring, tak-
ing pains; (the neut. may be used impersonally,
e. g. यतितम् मया गन्तुम्, it was attempted by
me to go, it was my intention to go.)

यतितव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be strived for or after,
to be endeavoured; (the neut. is used impersonally
with loc., e. g. अर्थार्जने यतितव्यम्, one must
strive for the acquisition of money.)

यतुन, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. going, moving, (Sāy. =
गन्तृ.)
यतुन यतुन. See p. 804, col.3.

1. यत्त, अस्, आ, अम् (for 2. see under rt. यम्),
endeavoured, making effort or exertion, taking care,
watchful; prepared, ready; ready for (e. g. रणे
यत्तः, ready for battle, or with an inf.); resolved;
cared for, attended to (as a chariot, &c.).

2. यत्त, अस्, आ, अम् (for 1. see p. 804, col. 3), =
यत, col. 1, (occurring rarely in ep. poetry, and only
when required by the exigency of metre.)
यत यत. See under rt. यम्, p. 809.

यत, अस्, आ, अम्, restrained, held in, curbed,
kept in check, governed, &c.; limited, moderate,
temperate; (अम्), n. the spurring or guiding of an
elephant by means of the rider's feet.
—यत-गिर्,
ईर्, ईर्, ईर्, one who restrains speech, keeping silence;
[cf. यत-वाच्.]
—यतङ्-कर, अस्, m., Ved. one
who regulates, a regulator, (Sāy. = यमन-कर्तृ.)
—यत-चित्त, अस्, आ, अम्, one who controls the
thoughts or restrains the feelings, subdued in mind.
—यतचित्तात्मन् (˚त-आत्˚), आ, आ, अ, one who con-
trols the soul and spirit, of subdued or well-governed
mind.
—यत-मन्यु, उस्, उस्, उ, restraining or con-
trolling anger.
—यत-मानस, अस्, आ, अम्, = यत-
चित्त above.
—यत-मैथुन, अस्, आ, अम्, abstain-
ing from sexual intercourse or restraining all desire
for it.
—यत-रश्मि, इस्, इस्, इ, Ved. having well
held or guided reins.
—यतवाक्-त्व, अम्, n. the
state of being restrained in speech, reticence.
—यत-
वाच्, क्, क्, क्, restraining speech, observing silence,
reticent.
—यत-व्रत, अस्, आ, अम्, observing vows,
keeping to engagements, holding to any promised
observance.
—यत-स्रुच्, क्, क्, क्, Ved. raising or
lifting up the sacrificial ladle, stretching out or extend-
ing the ladle; [cf. उद्यत-स्रुच्.]
—यतात्मन् (˚त-
आत्˚), आ, आ, अ, self-restrained, restraining or curbing
the soul, governing one's self.
—यतात्म-वत्, आन्,
अती, अत्, having a subdued mind, self-restrained.
—य-
ताहार (˚त-आह्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, abstaining from food,
temperate in eating, abstemious.
—यतेन्द्रिय (˚त-
इन्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, having the organs of sense restrained,
of subdued passions, chaste, pure.

यात, अस्, आ, अम्, gone, proceeded, marched,
passed, &c.; gone to, attained, obtained (with acc.);
passed by or away, elapsed, escaped; (अम्), n. the
act of going, going, march, proceeding; motion,
(often confounded with यान, q. v.); the past time
(e. g. यातम् अनागतं च, the past and the
future); the guiding or driving of an elephant with
a goad.
—यात-याम, अस्, आ, अम्, or यात-यामन्,
आ, आ, अ, that which has completed its course or (ac-
cording to others) that which has stood for a night
(and so become flat and stale), used, spoiled, im-
paired, useless, rejected; raw, half ripe; who or
what has run out or completed a course, exhausted,
old, aged.
—यातयाम-त्व, अम्, n. uselessness,
unprofitableness; old age.
—यातानुयात (˚त-अन्˚),
अम्, n. the going and following.
—यातायात (˚त-
आय्˚) or यातोपयात (˚त-उप्˚), अम्, n. a going and
coming; intercourse.
—यातोपयातिक, see Gaṇa
Akṣa-dyūtādi to Pāṇ.
यात यात, &c. See p. 813, col. 2.

यत्न, अस्, m. effort, endeavour, exertion, energy,
diligence, perseverance, zeal; labour, work, trouble,
pains, difficulty; effort for, endeavour after (with
loc., e. g. परोपकृतौ यत्नः, an effort for the
benefit of another); यत्नं कृ, to make effort,
use exertion, take pains, strive; (एन), ind. with
effort, diligently, vigorously, eagerly, with all one's
might; carefully; (आत्), ind. from effort, with effort,
after great exertions; in spite of every effort; neces-
sarily.
—यत्न-तस्, ind. from effort, diligently, vigo-
rously, eagerly, zealously; carefully.
—यत्न-प्रति-
पाद्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be explained with difficulty,
difficult, not easy.
—यत्न-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, pos-
sessing energy, making or using effort, energetic,
using exertion, strenuous, laborious, assiduous, perse-
vering, diligent; striving after, taking pains about
(with loc.).
—यत्नवत्-त्व, अम्, n. the state or
condition of making effort, diligence, zealousness.
—यत्नाक्षेप (˚न-आक्˚), अस्, m. (in rhetoric) the
making an objection notwithstanding an effort to
repress it.
यत्न यत्न, यत्य, &c. See p. 804, col. 3.

यत्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be strived for or after, to
be exerted.

यात्य यात्य, अस्, m. (fr. the Caus. of rt.
2. यत्), ‘to be tormented, subject to the torments of
hell,’ an inhabitant of hell, a condemned spirit.

यतम यतम, अस्, आ, अत् (superl. of 3. य or
यद्; see
Gram. 236
), who or which (of many).

यतमथा, ind., Ved. in which of many ways,
(यतमथा कतमथा, in the same way, as
always.)

यतर, अस्, आ, अत् (compar. of 3. य), who or
which (of two).
यतरथा, ind. in which of two ways.

यतस् यतस्, ind. (fr. the pronom. base
3. य; correlative of ततस्, q. v., and often used
for the ablative or even instrumental cases यस्मात्,
येभ्यस्, यस्यास्, येन, &c. of the relative pronoun
यद्, but oftener as an adverb or conjunction), from
which, from what, whence; in consequence of
which, for which reason, wherefore; because, since,
whereas, as, for; from which place, wherefrom,
from any place; where, whither, in which direction;
from which time, from which time forward, ever
since, (यतो जाता, from her birth up to the present
time, ever since her birth); that, so that, on con-
dition that; यतो-यतस्, from whichever, from
whatever, from whatever place, from wherever,
whencesoever, wherever, whithersoever; यतस्-ततस्,
from whichever, from which place soever, from this
or that person or place, from any one whatever,
from any place whatsoever, any whither, any where-
soever; यत एव कुतश् च, from this or that place,
from any place whatever; यतः-प्रभृति, whence-
[]
forward, from which time forward, from what time;
[cf. Gr. ὅ-θε-ν; Slav. jundu-se.]
—यतो-जा, आस्,
आस्, अम्, or यतोद्भव (˚तस्-उद्˚), अस्, आ, अम्,
produced from which.
—यतो-मूल, अस्, आ, अम्, ori-
ginating in or from which.

यति 1. यति (fr. the pronom. base 3. य;
correlative of तति, q. v.; declined in plur. only, all
the cases except the nom. voc. acc. taking termina-
tions, e. g. inst. यतिभिस्, dat. and abl. यतिभ्यस्,
gen. यतीनाम्, loc. यतिषु, see
Gram. 227

. a),
as many (= Lat. quot); as often; how many; how
often. (For 2. यति see p. 809, col. 1.)

2. यति, इस्, f. (for 1. see p. 805, col. 1), restraint,
control, check; guidance; stopping, ceasing, rest,
term; a pause (in music); cæsura (in prosody); a
widow, (in this sense also यती; cf. यतिनी); (इस्),
m. an ascetic, devotee, one who has restrained his
passions and abandoned the world; N. of a mythical
race of ascetics (connected with the Bhṛgus and,
[]
according to one legend, said to have taken part in
the creation of the world); N. of a son of Brahmā;
of a son of Nahuṣa; of a son of Viśvāmitra; (with
Jainas) N. of a class of ascetics; N. of Śiva; =
निकार.
—यति-चान्द्रायण, अम्, n., N. of a par-
ticular kind of penance (Manu

).
—यति-
त्व, अम्, n. the state of a Yati or ascetic.
—यति-
धर्म, अस्, m. the duty of an ascetic or devotee.
—यति-धर्मन्, आ, m., N. of a son of Śva-phalka.
—यतिधर्म-समुच्चय, अस्, m., N. of a work
on the duties of ascetics.
—यति-पञ्चक, अम्, n.,
N. of five stanzas on the subject of ascetics.
—यति-
पात्र, अम्, n. an ascetic's vessel, a wooden vessel
for collecting alms, (sometimes a hollow bamboo or
an earthen bowl or a gourd is used for that purpose.)
—यति-भ्रष्ट, अस्, आ, अम्, wanting the cæsura
(in grammar or prosody).
—यति-मैथुन, अम्, n.
the copulation or cohabitation of devotees, the un-
chaste life of ascetics.
—यति-वर्य, अस्, m., N.
of the author of a commentary on Śiro-maṇi's
Dīdhiti.
—यति-विलास, अस्, m. a proper N.
—यति-
सान्तपन, अम्, n., N. of a particular kind of
penance, (a पञ्च-गव्य lasting for three days.)
—यत्य्-अनुष्ठान-पद्धति, इस्, f., N. of a trea-
tise on the duties of ascetics by Śaṅkara Ānanda.
यती. See under 2. यति, col. 1.
याति, इस्, f. (said to be fr. the Intens.), see Pāṇ.

यतिथ, अस्, ई, अम्, ‘as maniest, the as manieth;’
[cf. ततिथ.]

यतिधा, ind., Ved. in as many parts, in as many
ways.
यतीयस यतीयस (?), अम्, n. silver.

यतुका यतुका or यतूका, f. a species of
plant (= रजनी, जननी).

यत्कर यत्-कर, यत्-काम, यत्-कारणम्,
यत्-क्रतु, &c. See p. 808, col. 1.

यत्र यत्र, ind. (fr. the pronom. base 3.
य; correlative of तत्र, q. v., often used for the
loc. cases यस्मिन्, यस्याम्, येषु, &c., but oftener
as an adverb or conjunction), in which place, where,
wherein, wherever, whither; when; whereas, be-
cause, since; that, so that; यत्र यत्र, wherever,
wheresoever, whithersoever, whensoever; यत्र-
तत्र, in any place whatever, anywhere, (यत्र-
तत्र दिने, on any day whatever, on whatever day
you like); यत्र-कुत्र, in any place whatever;
everywhere, in every part; यत्र-कुत्रचित् or यत्र-
कुत्रापि, in whatever place, in some place or other,
in any place whatever, anywhere, in whichever (e. g.
यत्र-कुत्रापि जन्मनि, in whichever birth); य-
त्र-क्वचन or यत्र-क्वापि or यत्र-क्व च or
यत्र-क्व वा, wherever, whithersoever, anywhere,
anywhither; whenever, as often as, every time; at
any time; hither and thither.
—यत्र-कामम्, ind.
wherever it pleases, according to pleasure or wish.
—यत्र-कामावसाय (˚म-अव्˚), अस्, m. the super-
natural power of taking up an abode or transporting
one's self anywhere one likes, (this power is said to
belong to some Yogins.)
—यत्रकामावसायि-ता,
f. or यत्रकामावसायि-त्व, अम्, n. = यत्र-कामा-
वसाय above.
—यत्रकामावसायिन्, ई, इनी, इ,
having the power of taking up a residence or trans-
porting one's self anywhere one wishes.
—यत्र-
तत्र-शय, अस्, आ, अम्, lying down anywhere, sleep-
ing anywhere.
—यत्र-सायङ्-गृह or यत्र-सा-
यम्-प्रतिश्रय, अस्, आ, अम्, having or taking up
an abode wherever the evening finds one, spending
the night anywhere where one happens to be.
—य-
त्र-स्थ, अस्, आ, अम्, where staying, in which place
abiding.
—यत्राकूत (˚र-आक्˚), अम्, n., Ved. the
aim or object in view.

यात्रा, f. going, setting off, journey, travel, march,
the march of an army, expedition, (यात्रां या or
दा, to undertake an expedition or campaign, take
the field); going on a pilgrimage; a company of
pilgrims; a festive train, procession, the procession
of idols; a feast, festival (= उत्सव); a sort of
dramatic entertainment; a road; support of life,
livelihood, subsistence, provisions; passing away time;
going to and fro; intercourse, (लौकिकी यात्रा or
जगद्-यात्रा, worldly intercourse); way, means, ex-
pedient; practice, usage, custom; N. of a particular
kind of astrological work (especially of one by Varāha-
mihira, the full title of which is Yoga-yātrā).
—या-
त्रा-करण, अम्, n. the setting forth on a journey,
a march.
—यात्रा-कार, अस्, m. the author of a work
of the Yātrā class.
—यात्रा-गमन, अम्, n. the
going on a journey or expedition.
—यात्रा-प्रसङ्ग,
अस्, m. engaging in or performing a pilgrimage.
—यात्रा-फल, अम्, n. the fruit of an expedition,
success of a campaign.
—यात्रा-महोत्सव (˚हा-
उत्˚), अस्, m. a great festive procession.
—यात्रार्-
थम् (˚रा-अर्˚), ind. for the sake of marching.
—या-
त्रोत्सव (˚रा-उत्˚), अस्, m. a festive procession.

यात्रा यात्रा, यात्रिक, &c. See p. 813,
col. 3.

यत्रत्य, अस्, आ, अम्, where being, dwelling in
which place, relating to which place, of which place,
whose (used relatively).
यतिन्, ई, m. = 2. यति, an ascetic; (इनी), f. a widow.

यत्वा, ind. having restrained, having curbed or
controlled.

यातिक, अस्, m. a traveller, (probably incorrect for
यात्रिक.)

1. यातु, 3rd sing. Impv. of rt. 1. या above (often
used as an interjection), let it go, let it pass, be it so,
no matter.

2. यातु, उस्, उस्, उ, a goer, one who goes or
moves; (उस्), m. a traveller, wayfarer; wind; time;
(perhaps) sorcery, witchcraft, (but according to Sāy.
[]
यातु means either कर्मणां हिंसा, injury of rites,
or पीडा, pain, torture); a kind of evil spirit, Rākṣasa,
demon; (उ), n. a weapon, (according to Sāy. as
inflicting यातना, pain); a Rākṣasa, evil spirit,
demon.
—यातु-घ्न, अस्, ई, अम्, destroying Yātus;
(अस्), m. bdellium.
—यातु-चातन, अस्, ई, अम्, Ved.
‘Yātu-removing,’ driving away Rākṣasas.
—यातु-
